name: 3 Toppsløpet Jeløya
description: The 3toppsløpet on Jeløy was held for the first time in 2014 and is a trail run that takes you through some of the most beautiful places on Jeløy. You can run four different distances: 1 km, 10 km, 20 km, or 30 km. The race is a true test of strength and a relatively challenging and technically demanding trail run, where runners alternate between running along the beaches and on forest paths. The goal of the race is to create as nice a route as possible around the entire Jeløy, passing over the three well-known peaks: Rødsåsen, Bjørnåsen, and Rambergtoppen.
course_highlights: The runners alternate between running along the beaches and on trails in the forest on beautiful Jeløy.
Every year, the organizers donate the profits from the trail race to charity and aid work.

name: Besseggløpet
description: Besseggen is one of Norway's most beautiful hiking destinations. The Besseggen Race follows the regular T-marked route over the ridge. Start at Memurubu and finish at the Gjendeosen parking area. The terrain is rugged, mainly gravel and stone. There will typically also be some snow in parts of the trail. The start and finish are at about 1000 meters above sea level, with the highest point at approximately 1743 meters above sea level. The course is about 14 km long.
course_highlights: The course is approximately 14 km long, with an elevation difference of 1000 m.
The terrain is uneven, primarily gravel and stone, and there will usually be some snow in parts of the trail.
The Besseggløpet is held every last Saturday in June, offering opportunities for both recreational runners and competitive athletes.

Here, both adults and children can participate in various distances, including marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and a "Miniton" of 4.2 km. The courses run along Jølstravatnet, and there are opportunities for both competition and fitness. Awards are presented at the finish line, and result lists will be available at Jølstrahallen.
course_highlights: Jølster Marathon is one of Norway's most traditional races!
The trails run through beautiful West Coast nature.
The top three in each class/distance will be awarded.

Runners in the Jølster Marathon run through beautiful Norwegian nature.

name: Bitihorn Opp
description: Welcome to an informal and casual uphill race up Bithihorn. Whether you walk or run, fast or slow, everyone is welcome. The course runs on stone steps and trails on the front side of Bithorn, with a distance of 2 kilometers and an elevation gain of 450 meters. The race takes place on Saturday, July 5, 2025, starting at 12:00 PM, and there will be prizes, good vibes, and spectacular views at the top.
course_highlights: The course is approximately 2 km with 450 meters of elevation gain and is suitable for both hikers and competitive runners.
The hike to the top of Bitihorn offers magnificent views of Jotunheimen and large parts of Valdres.
It is a moderately challenging summit hike with a clear trail and no special difficulties.

images.alt_text: Bitihorn summit hike! Happy hikers are enjoying the view. #BitihornUp #Beitostølen

name: Ålgård-Sirdal 100K
description: Ålgård-Sirdal 100K is a challenging course of 100 kilometers that takes participants from Ålgård to Sirdal. The route is varied, featuring both mountains and roads, and the last aid station is at Lortabu (86 km). After this, the course follows the road to Gravassryggen, before ascending the steep trail to Storeknut. Towards the end of the race, participants will experience a fantastic view over Sirdal from the finish line at Slottet.
course_highlights: The last aid station is at Lortabu (86 km), where the route then follows the road to Gravassryggen.
After 90 km, the participants will understand why the trail gets its name from the 1800s, when shepherds had to herd their sheep from the coast to the mountain pastures in Sirdal.
About 1 km before the finish, there is a steep gravel path leading to the finish at the Castle, where you get a fantastic view of the entire Sirdal.

Snow-covered mountain road with cars in a winter landscape.

name: Rødtangen Rundt
description: Rødtangen Rundt 2024 was a success! With 144 participants in the main race and 55 participants in the children's races, we have reached levels from before the pandemic. The event took place in beautiful Holmsbu, and both young and old experienced the joy of participating in the race.
course_highlights: 144 participants in the main race.
55 participants in the children’s races.
The event brings us back to the level we were at before the pandemic.

name: Preikestolen Trailrun
description: The Preikestolen Trailrun is an epic running journey where you follow in the footsteps of Rockman, the legendary figure who braved the rugged trails every weekend in pursuit of winning his beloved's heart, but without swimming. This race is not just a run – it is a mythical adventure where you battle against the forces of nature on some of the world's most spectacular trails. Prepare for a mix of skyrunning, technical trail running, and exhilarating climbing, as you run through mystical forests, cross boulder fields, and ascend to the mountain peaks above the Lysefjord. The route takes you on a secret path to the iconic Preikestolen, before descending into a playground of ancient, rugged terrain.
course_highlights: You will run through mystical forests, cross moors, and ascend to the mountain peaks above the Lysefjord, where the shimmering water is framed by majestic cliffs.
The route takes you along a secret outer trail to the iconic Preikestolen, before descending into a playground of ancient, rugged terrain – shaped by the gods themselves.
This race is extremely technical with an elevation gain of 1200 meters and a distance of 20 km.

images.alt_text: Preikestolen, Lysefjord, Norway. Amazing hike with a view over the fjord.
View over the Lysefjord from Preikestolen. Two people are sitting and looking out over the beautiful landscape.
Runner on the trail towards Lysefjorden. Preikestolen Trailrun logo.
Runners in a cross-country race, with Norwegian flags on their clothing.

name: Jomfrulandsløpet
description: The Jomfruland Race is open to everyone, including those who are not affiliated with a sports club. The "classic" race is 10 km long, consisting of two laps on a 5-kilometer course. It is also possible to participate in one lap, which is 5 km with timing. The course is on flat ground, gravel, and forest trails, and it all takes place on the beautiful island of Jomfruland off the coast of Kragerø.
course_highlights: The race is open to everyone, including those who are not affiliated with a sports club.
The "classic" Jomfrulandsløpet is 10 km long and consists of two laps in a 5-kilometer course.
The course is on flat ground, gravel, and forest trails.

name: Feriespretten
description: Feriespretten is a traditional trail race that has been organized by Hope IL for 34 years. The race features two distances: a long course of approximately 9 km and a short course of about 5 km, both set in varied, hilly terrain. It is scheduled for Tuesday, July 9, 2024, at 5:59 PM (GMT+2) in Sandnes, Norway, with a mass start and 135 participants. Feriespretten is known for its festive atmosphere, even in challenging weather conditions such as rain.
course_highlights: The race has attracted both young and experienced runners, and there has been a record number of participants this year.
Trim trail: If you don't want to be timed, you can still participate as a recreational runner in the short course.
The race is timed using RFID technology and utilizes Webscorer PRO 6.9 for the results.

name: Dream Challenge
description: The inspiring charity race Dream Challenge takes place in Lillesand on Saturday, July 13. Dream Challenge is not just a race, but also a fundraising campaign where all proceeds go directly to Star for Life's work with youth in South Africa – training with purpose. We encourage everyone to participate on this day, where we combine physical activity with support for a good cause. This is an event for the whole family! Bring friends and family and join as runners, support crew, or cheer squad.
course_highlights: All funds go directly to Star for Life's work with youth in South Africa – training with purpose.
This is an event for the whole family!
Together we can make a difference for youth in South Africa.

name: Oslo Bergen Trail
description: Oslo Bergen Trail is a trail ultramarathon from Oslo to Bergen, taking place from July 2-10, 2021. The course is approximately 515 km long with a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters, and follows marked hiking trails (DNT trails) where possible and appropriate. In some short sections, the route goes through forest and mountain terrain without a trail or follows only a faint track. The organizer may activate alternate routes under difficult weather conditions.
course_highlights: The route follows marked hiking trails (DNT trails) where possible and appropriate.
The course is approximately 515 km long with a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters.
This is a team competition where each team can consist of 2 or 3 people.

name: Brunlanesløpet
description: The Brunlanesløpet is organized by Brunlanes IL and starts and finishes outside Nesjarhallen in Helgeroa. The courses run through easy terrain, mostly on gravel roads and trails in beautiful natural areas near Nevlunghavn, Mølen, and Helgeroa. In 2025, the race will take place on July 12, with the children's race starting at 12:30, the Gåløypen at 13:00, the 4.6 km at 13:00, and the 9.0 km at 13:10.
course_highlights: The routes go through easy terrain, mostly on gravel roads and trails in beautiful natural areas.
The Brunlanes Race 2025 will be held on July 12, 2025.
The start and finish are outside Nesjarhallen in Helgeroa.

name: Kvasshovden Opp
description: Kvasshovden Opp is a mountain running race organized by Ulvik Idrettslag, which was first held in 2008. The race has since become a great success, with over 500 participants in 2009 and has been part of the Powerade Norwegian Cup in mountain running. The course starts in the center of Ulvik at about 10 meters above sea level and finishes at the top of Kvasshovden, 1030 meters above sea level, over a distance of 7.5 km. At the top, a fantastic view of the western Norwegian fjord landscape awaits.
course_highlights: The course has a length of 7.5 km and ascends from 0 to 1030 m.a.s.l.
The race is known for its steep and rocky terrain, and the record from the center to the top is under an hour.
Participants can enjoy a spectacular view of the fjord landscape from the top, as well as pass several beautiful mountain pasture areas and local farms along the way.

name: Risberget Rundt
description: Risberget Rundt is a trail run organized by the Risberget Hiking Association every year in July. The routes are well marked, so you can also walk Risberget Rundt on your own throughout the summer season. You can choose between a 5 km and an 11 km loop, making it an ideal family outing. The start and finish are at Kynnbrua.
course_highlights: The trails are marked in the spring so that you can also walk around Risberget on your own throughout the summer months.
You can choose between a 5 km and an 11 km loop.
The start and finish are at Kynnbrua.

name: Hardangerjøkulen Ultra
description: In just over three weeks, I will be running the Hardangerjøkulen ultra. It is a new race on the calendar and has only previously been held as a trial race in 2018. I included it in my race calendar for two main reasons: Hardangervidda is incredibly beautiful, and it is an area I have never run in before. The race is 100 km long with about 2500 meters of elevation gain, starting and finishing in Eidfjord.
course_highlights: The race is 100 km long with approximately 2500 meters of elevation gain.
There is a new race on the calendar, which was only previously held as a trial run in 2018.
Hardangervidda is absolutely beautiful, and it's an area I have never run in before.

name: Espe Rundt
description: Espe Rundt is a 7 km fitness run held every week from Easter to moose hunting season, with a mass start at 6:00 PM every Thursday from Nordåsveien 43 in Birkeland. The course goes up Nordåsstien, continues towards Haugevann, and around Espe before returning to the start. Participation is free of charge, but a small fee is required for prizes in the final race. All results are published on the Espe Rundt Facebook page and in Birkenesavisa.
course_highlights: The course is exactly 7050 m, and the record is held by Hans Gunnar Omdal from Vindbjart with a time of 28:51 set on July 1, 2004.
There is room for everyone who wants a nice trip on a very special course, and the race is best suited for the fit hiker or runner.
You must have completed 3 races to be counted in the final, which is a reverse chase start based on the average of your three best races throughout the summer.

name: Bislett Distanseserie
description: The Bislett Distance Series is a low-threshold running carousel aimed at organizing one race per month at Bislett Stadium. Here, a welcoming environment is created for participation, top conditions, and a fantastic atmosphere. Join us and kickstart the running season indoors at the historic Bislett Stadium! Participants will enjoy a fantastic running experience with nuts and bars, sports drinks from Maxim, and the opportunity to run alongside others at their level.
course_highlights: A fantastic running experience at Bislett Stadium.
Nuts and bars for all registered participants.
The opportunity to run together with others at your level.

name: Skjernøyløpet
description: Welcome to Norway's southernmost race – the Skjernøyløpet – which takes place on Thursday, July 25, 2024, at 6:00 PM, with bib number pickup starting at 5:00 PM. The course is 6 km and runs around Skjernøy in Mandal. This race is for both young and old who want to challenge themselves on this tough and fun course.
course_highlights: The Skjernøy Race is an annual event on the 6 km course around Skjernøy in Mandal.
The race has a mass start and is a road race.
In 2017, 69 participants took part in the race.

name: Preikestolen Trailrun
description: Get ready for an unforgettable adventure at the Preikestolen Trailrun, organized by Rockman on Saturday, July 5, 2025, in the stunning location of Jørpeland, Strand. This epic trail race invites you to conquer a challenging 20 km route with an impressive elevation gain of 1200 meters, as you follow the legendary paths of Rockman himself. Participants will experience a mythical journey through the enchanting landscapes of the Lysefjord, with mystical forests, rock piles, and dramatic mountain peaks. The race culminates at the iconic Preikestolen, offering breathtaking views over the shimmering waters and majestic cliffs.
course_highlights: Participants will experience a mythical journey through the enchanting landscapes of Lysefjorden, with mysterious forests, stone piles, and dramatic mountain peaks.
The race culminates at the iconic Preikestolen, which offers stunning views over the sparkling waters and majestic cliffs.
This is not just a race; it is a test of endurance and spirit against the forces of nature.

name: Kvitfjell Opp
description: Kvitfjell Opp is one of the summer's most brutal uphill races, where we turn the Olympic course upside down and run from the finish at the bottom to the start at the top. The course is 3.2 kilometers long with an elevation gain of 838 meters, following the downhill track used during the 1994 Olympics. Participants will encounter challenging sections such as Mæhlumshenget, Tommy Moe, and Wintherhugget, and the feeling of reaching the top is indescribable!
course_highlights: The course follows the downhill track that was used during the 1994 Olympics and is currently used in connection with the World Cup.
The course features challenging sections such as Mæhlumshenget, Tommy Moe, and Wintherhugget, with inclines of up to 50%.
Kvitfjell Opp is a real challenge for most, but also a manageable task that provides a fantastic sense of accomplishment.

name: Blefjells Beste
description: Blefjells Beste is a social and informal race for everyone who enjoys training in forest and mountain areas. The race starts and finishes at the private cabin Bestebu, located by Klengstøl along Store-Bleveien. We offer several courses: Troll Course 57 km with 2000 m elevation gain, Storetroll Course 93 km with 3200 m elevation gain, Tusse Course 21 km with 750 m elevation gain, Småtusse Course 10 km with 340 m elevation gain, and Småtroll Course 5 km with 110 m elevation gain. The courses primarily follow trails.
course_highlights: We offer the following courses: Troll Trail 57 km, 2000 m elevation gain.
Storetroll Trail 93 km, 3200 m elevation gain.
The trails primarily run on paths.

name: Kvitfjell Stuttlaup
description: Stuttlaupet is a 13 km long race in varied terrain, taking place during the Kvitfjell Running Festival. The festival, which was established in 2022, also includes other races such as Kvitfjell Opp and Langlaupet. In 2024, the festival will expand with Stuttlaupet, which will provide participants with a fantastic experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Stuttlaupet is a 13 km long race in varied terrain.
Kvitfjell Running Festival will be held on July 26 and 27, with the Short Run at 10:00 AM on July 27.
The festival also includes a banquet dinner and an afterparty following the race.

name: Kvitfjell Langlaup
description: The long run is a 25 km race in varied terrain, presenting an extra challenge for those who didn't get enough lactic acid from Friday's uphill race. The course mainly follows marked trails in the mountain area around Kvitfjell, and the race takes place both above and below the tree line, with the highest point at about 1100 meters above sea level. Even though it is mid-summer, it can be wise to be prepared for weather changes.
course_highlights: Kvitfjell Running Festival has been delivering legendary running experiences since 2021, featuring Northern Europe's steepest ski slope and prime trails in the heart of Norwegian nature.
The course is approximately 25 kilometers long, with 19 kilometers on trails and 6.5 kilometers on road.
In 2024, the festival will expand with yet another race, namely the Stuttlaupet.

name: Jordbærdilten
description: The Strawberry Run and the Mini Run are two separate races taking place in Valldal. The Mini Run starts at 2:45 PM, while the Strawberry Run starts at 3:30 PM. Both races have their start and finish at Rådhusmarka, and there will be an awards ceremony at the pier after the race.
course_highlights: The mini race starts at 2:45 PM.
The Strawberry Run starts at 3:30 PM.
Start and finish at Rådhusmarka, with award ceremony at the quay.

name: Sørlandstesten 11
description: The Sørlandstest is a low-threshold recreational race for everyone who wants a positive running experience, regardless of ambition level. Whether you are training for a bigger goal, feeling the competitive nerves, or just want a social and active day – this is the race for you! There is room for both beginners and experienced runners, and the most important thing is that you show up with a good mood and a desire to run. We cheer just as much for the one who crosses the finish line first as for the one who completes their very first race.
course_highlights: The Sørlandstest offers a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai, before participants turn around and run back.
The race features distances of 5 km, 10 km, and a 600 m children's race, making it accessible for all ages and skill levels.
The start and finish are located on the opposite side of the road from Gumpens Auto, providing a simple and accessible location in Kristiansand.

name: Løp til Verdens Ende
description: Run to the World's End is a duathlon where teams of two run trail and swim in open water, without a break between the two disciplines. The running distance is longer than a full marathon, in addition to eight kilometers in the water. According to the organizer, this is a fantastic way to utilize the archipelago, but there is no room for transitions between the two activities, so participants must run and swim in wetsuits and running shoes. It is recommended to use flotation devices to make it easier.
course_highlights: Duathlon with trail running and open water swimming without breaks between the disciplines.
The race distance is longer than a full marathon, in addition to eight kilometers of swimming.
Participants must wear a wetsuit and running shoes, and it is recommended to use flotation devices.

name: Kongsvinger Skogsmaraton
description: Kongsvinger Forest Marathon is Inland's only and Norway's second forest marathon, taking place on August 3, 2024. Here you can choose from many different distances, including the full marathon, half marathon, and Kongsvingermila. Experience an unforgettable day filled with joy, community, and competition in a hilly and varied forest area north and west of Sæter farm. The marathon course follows forest roads and good trails, and there are 3 aid stations along the route.
course_highlights: Kongsvinger Forest Marathon offers distances of 42.2 km, 21.1 km, 10 km, and 4.2 km.
The marathon route runs through a hilly, varied, and beautiful forest area, with the main course following forest roads and good trails.
There are 3 water stations set up for participants during the race.

name: Gaea Norvegica Trail
description: Gaea Norvegica Trail is a multi-day, self-supported race, known as Norway's longest and toughest ultra. There are two routes: the first is 400 kilometers long and the second is 600 kilometers long, both completed over a 5-day period. The race is ITRA-certified and offers 6 UTMB points. Are you brave enough to take on nature and see how you fare? Join us and experience the stunning beauty of Norwegian nature while following the geological Oslo Rift formation from Oslo to Hamar.
course_highlights: The route follows the Akerselva river to Maridalsvannet, continues into Nordmarka up to Eidsvoll, and then heads northeast before ending at Hedmarksvidda.
The total elevation gain in the race is 8300 meters, and assistance is not allowed; participants must carry all clothing, food, and drink in their backpacks.
Gaea Norvegica Trail is ITRA-certified and offers 6 UTMB points, making it a challenging experience for ultrarunners.

name: Møkster Maraton
description: Welcome to Møkster Marathon! The race takes place on Saturday, August 9, 2025, and this is the 13th time the event is being held. Møkster is a beautiful, small island at the edge of the sea, located in Austevoll municipality south of Bergen. Here, participants can experience stunning nature, a guest harbor, a shop, and a restaurant. The routes traverse fields and roads, asphalt and gravel, through farmyards and along old farm roads, providing an absolutely extraordinary experience.
course_highlights: Møkster Marathon was held for the first time on Saturday, August 4, 2012, and it became an unforgettable day for organizers, spectators, and runners.
The race goes over fields and roads, asphalt and gravel, through farmyards and along old farm roads.
Møkster is a small island with about 35 permanent residents and a large group of cabin owners, all with a high percentage of passionate individuals.

description: Jotunheimen Trail Run - The ultimate experience of trail running. Choose between 13KM, 21KM, Ultra, or join the Kids' Race. Welcome to Jotunheimen Trail Run - An experience you won't forget!
course_highlights: Choose between 13KM / 21KM / Ultra or join the Children's Race.

name: Skeikampen Rundt
description: Skeikampen Rundt is a trail run set in scenic surroundings of small forests and bare mountains around Skeikampen. The course is approximately 12.2 km long and ascends to 347 meters, and it can be run in either direction, with a descent regardless of the route chosen. The run is moderately challenging and suitable for children, but everyone must enjoy downhill runs. It offers fantastic views of the mountain landscape, including Jotunheimen and Rondane, and concludes with waffles and coffee at one of the cozy mountain cafés.
course_highlights: The trail ascends to the trail junction at Torsdalsleitet, where you get a fantastic view of the surrounding mountains.
The trip is moderately challenging and suitable for children, but everyone must enjoy downhill runs.
The end of the race offers waffles and coffee at the atmospheric Skeistua mountain cafe or Nystua cafe.

name: Trysil Trail
description: Experience trail running, community, and mountain adventures in Trysil! Trysil Trail by HOKA is organized in collaboration with Marathongruppen, ensuring a professional and seamless experience from start to finish. Trysil Trail is more than just a race – it’s a weekend filled with after-run activities, social runs, training sessions, and an equipment fair. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced runner, inspiring experiences and nature encounters await you in the spectacular mountain landscape.
course_highlights: Trysil Trail is not just race day – it’s a weekend of running, community, and incredible experiences.
The weekend offers camaraderie, after run, and memorable experiences, in addition to two races through beautiful terrain.
Trysil Trail 14K starts in Fageråsen and follows the Mountain Loop, while the 24K has an additional detour around Skrufjellet.

name: Bodøryggen
description: Bodø Run Bodøryggen, which takes place on Saturday, October 1st, is a majestic mountain race of approximately 21 kilometers from Skaug to Bestemorenga in Bodømarka. This race offers a beautiful trail with fantastic views of the Vestfjord, Lofoten Wall, and the city of Bodø. Bodøryggen is a challenging yet rewarding journey with about 1,000 meters of elevation gain, perfect for experienced hikers looking for a memorable experience.
course_highlights: Start at Skaug, steeply up to Skaugtuva before it levels out and the journey can be enjoyed along Bodøryggen / Løpsfjellet.
Bodøryggen offers a spectacular view of the Vestfjord, the Lofoten Wall, the city of Bodø, and Børvasstindan.

The first lap starts at 09:00, with 1 hour between each lap, and the twelfth and final lap starts at 20:00. If no one finishes the last lap, there are no winners. If multiple participants complete all laps, the winner is the one who crosses the finish line first in the last lap.

name: Mjøsen Backyard Race
description: With 12 laps and a total of 2856 meters of elevation gain, Mjøsen Backyard takes you through a challenge equivalent to running from the deepest point of Lake Mjøsa up to the water surface six times. This is the race for you who want to challenge both body and willpower, and experience the joy of mastering one of Norway's most unique racing concepts. How long can you keep moving? The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long your break is before the next start.
course_highlights: Mjøsen Backyard is a backyard race consisting of laps of 6.7 km that are run up to twelve times.
The race starts and ends at a gathering place with a refreshment station, restrooms, and a chair to sit on.

This race is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful in Norway, but also one of the toughest, with a focus on all participants being winners, where the sense of achievement and the experience of nature are more important than the time. The event has an informal and social atmosphere, with a high enjoyment factor and a medal for everyone who finishes.

A total of 25 runners and cyclists participated, but only four women lined up at the start, with Ingunn Monsen being the fastest among them at 1:45:46. The organizers describe the course as Norway's most beautiful half marathon route and believe the race has the potential to grow in size.

Runners take to the track under the floodlights and compete in the 5K distance on iconic tracks around the world. name: Mud Monkey 2025
description:
MUDMONKEY 2025

Welcome to the Jungle. Play Dirty. Laugh Louder.

Mud. Obstacles. Screams and laughter. This is not a race – this is the jungle's playground for adults (and teenagers who aren't afraid to slip in style).

MudMonkey 2025 invites you to a day of total bananas in nature: climbing, crawling, water, fire, and a bunch of race-crazy Monkeys who live to challenge you through the course. Forget asphalt and fences – here you face the jungle's resistance with a grin.

MUDMONKEY 5K – “Monkey Business in Battle Mode”

5 kilometers with 25 technical and natural obstacles. 
You climb, tumble, crawl, and laugh your way through the mud while unruly MudMonkeys try to block you – physically. 
Go solo or as a tribe – but one thing is for sure: You will emerge covered in mud and full of adrenaline.

Age limit: 13+

A parental declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

MUDMONKEY 8K – “Mud Mayhem and Jungle Fury”

8 kilometers. 40+ obstacles.

When you think it can't get wilder, you arrive here. 
This is the highlight of the obstacle race: mud pits, zip lines, icy water, flames, slippery stones – and of course, crazy MudMonkeys trying to topple you with laughter and resistance.

Age limit: 16+

A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

____________________________________________________________________________________

COMING 2026 – MUDMONKEY EXTREME 21K

“For those who have never been dirty enough”

21 km. 70+ obstacles. Here you will meet your limits – and have them shattered.

Spectator-friendly, but participant-hostile course full of fire, ice, mud, and monkey madness.

Only for the most bananas among us.

Age limit: 18+
A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

EVERYONE GETS A MEDAL – NO ONE GOES HOME DRY OR CLEAN!!

Here, competition is held in individual classes and in tribes (teams). 
The fastest will be celebrated with honor and glory – but everyone who finishes gets a medal and the right to call themselves a true MudMonkey.
additional: Feel free to call us at 95961803 or send an email to hei@xchallenge.no.

name: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest
description: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is an ultramarathon held in the mountains of Bergen on the last weekend of August. The course, which stretches approximately 45 km from Gullbotn to Kjøkkelvik, has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters and includes several peaks such as Gullfjellstoppen and Ulriken. Since its inception in 1984, this event has become an annual tradition for many running enthusiasts, with course records of 4 hours and 40 minutes for men and 6 hours and 3 minutes for women. In 2023, Styrkeprøven Rett Vest celebrated its 35th anniversary.
course_highlights: The route starts at Gullbotn and ascends to the summit of Gullfjell, which is the highest point of the route at 987 meters.
The course has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters, providing a challenging and scenic experience.
Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is composed of volunteer members focused on creating a healthy and motivating activity event.

Four distances are offered: Long Trail 27 km (Black), Middle Trail 17 km (Red), Short Trail 7 km (Blue), and Raspberry Trail 1 km. All distances finish at Nermo Hotel, and the race follows the Pilgrims' Trail from Fjøssystemer (Sør-Fåvang) to Øyer.

name: Hodlekve Fjelløp
description: Join the mountain race of a lifetime! Hodlekve Rundt takes place on Saturday, September 24, and offers distances of 21 km, 10 km, and 6 km in beautiful terrain. This is the fourth year the race is being organized, and the routes follow marked trails. The activity day in Hodlekve will have offerings for both young and old, with a junior race, a treasure hunt, and sales of coffee and food at Dalalåven, which is open from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM.

description: The Oslo Running Festival consists of eight races along the capital's beautiful trails and scenic roads. You can run whenever you want – alone or together with others, either in the SOLO category or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO. Each race is announced on Friday at 12:00, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 the following weekend, with a mass start precisely at 11:00. The course is certified to be as close to 10 km as possible.
course_highlights: You can participate alone in the SOLO class, or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO.
Each race is scheduled to be announced on Friday at 12:00 PM, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 AM the following weekend.

description: The Røykenmila is a race that aims to create value in the local community and serves as an activity day for the whole family. The event has three goals: to create a festive day for everyone together with businesses and local associations, to motivate people to start training, and to raise money for good causes in the local community. There is an inclusive atmosphere with awards for participants in the 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as activities, booths, and entertainment for the entire family.
course_highlights: Røykenmila aims to create value in the local community and motivate people to start training.
The event includes activities for the whole family, with booths and entertainment.
There is an inclusive atmosphere with awards for participants in the 5 km and 10 km distances.

The trail goes through easy forest terrain and is approximately 1.5 km one way, with an elevation gain of about 200 meters. It takes about 45−60 minutes to complete and is suitable for children from around 5 years old.

The race takes place in Jessheim with a mass start, featuring a flat course of 3,146 meters. Participants can choose between distances ranging from 3 km to half marathon, including a fantastic children's race of 800 meters. The event has simple logistics, with parking and restrooms located 300 meters from the start, and self-service bib number pickup.
course_highlights: The race takes place on Sundays at 10:00 AM to make the execution as efficient as possible.
All distances start the same, which gives participants the opportunity to run alongside many others.
Participants receive a well-deserved medal after the race.

The start and finish are located across the road from Gumpens Auto, along Setesdalsveien in Kristiansand. Participants follow a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai, turn around, and run back the same way. If you're running 5 km, you turn around after passing 2.5 km. The course is officially measured, and the race is approved by and listed on NFIF's official schedule.

name: Flemstubben
description: The Flemstubben race is an annual road race held in Flemma, and this year it was conducted for the 44th time with 140 participants. The race has a distance of 10 kilometers, and Johan Bugge from Eidsvåg IL was the pre-race favorite, delivering a time of 30:52, just 6 seconds behind his own course record. Live Johannessen Solheimdal from Steinkjer FIK smashed her own record with an impressive time of 34:41, while Morten Eilifsen from Averøy Running Club achieved the second-best overall time with 34:35.

The route goes around Holavatnet on asphalt and gravel paths, and it is also possible to bring a stroller on the loop.

The start and finish are at the NaKuHel center, which also has Smia Café offering food and drinks. We hope for nice weather and a great atmosphere, so save the date for Wednesday, September 3rd!

We plan for participants to either walk or run, with or without timing, with categories for both competition and personal improvement.
There will be food and drink for sale at Smia Café, where you can buy waffles, cake, rolls, soda, and coffee.

The course is 8.6 km long, with 970 meters of positive elevation gain and 700 meters of negative elevation, and features exciting and challenging sections equipped with safety measures for secure passage.
course_highlights: The route offers a fantastic view with magnificent mountains such as Vengetindene, Romsdalshorn, and Trolltindene.
The course includes 4 different secured sections with chains to help participants navigate the challenging areas.
The exciting and challenging part begins when you reach the ridge, with 4.6 adrenaline-pumping kilometers remaining.

course_highlights: The race has a long history dating back to the early 1980s, with the first event in Blodslitet in 1982.

The race offers 42 kilometers through the capital and includes participation from runners, handcyclists, and wheelchair athletes.
course_highlights: BMW BERLIN-MARATHON allocates race spots by lottery.
42 zero-emission kilometers through the capital.
Runners, handbikers, and wheelchair athletes will start on Sunday.

name: Asker Spurten
description: AskerSpurten is an annual race aimed at raising funds for the Bamsefondet, so that more children and young people can participate in sports on equal terms. The races take place around Asker town center, and you can choose between 10 km, 5 km, or a 500 m children's race. Everyone is welcome! You can decide whether you want to run, jog, walk, or cycle the course you have chosen. The race starts with a group warm-up and the children's race, followed by the main races (5 km and 10 km) which begin with a mass start.
course_highlights: The races take place around Asker city center, and you can choose between 10 km, 5 km, or a 500 m children's race.
Everyone is welcome! You can choose whether you want to run, jog, walk, or cycle the course you have selected.

name: Trekktraseen Opp
description: Trekktraseen Up is a mountain race organized by Jølster Sports Club. The race takes place in Bjørkelia and has attracted many participants. It is known for its challenging uphill route, which offers participants a fantastic view of the area.
course_highlights: Sindre Hoff and Karoline Holsen Kyte both set new personal bests in their category on the challenging course in Jølster.
Sindre Hoff broke Bjarne Ness's old record of 6.33 by two seconds.
Karoline Holsen Kyte erased Ingrid Narum's nearly ten-year-old record when she reached the top at 8.24.

name: Nærsnes Backyard Run
description: Nærsnes Backyard is not about being first, but is a social low-threshold race held in Nærsnes. We have a great children's course and a larger adult course that caters to those who have never run before, to those who have run a little, to active runners. In the children's race, participation is the focus, and the event aims to be climate neutral and to serve as a pioneering race in terms of inclusion.
course_highlights: The event features a children's course and an adult course tailored to all levels, from beginners to active runners.
Participation is the focus in the children's race, promoting an inclusive atmosphere.
The race is designed to be climate neutral, with the aim of setting the standard for inclusion in running events.

name: Gjørmelabben Romerike
description: The Mud Paw is an unforgettable obstacle course for everyone with a dog, where all are welcome! The event is suitable for both individual teams, children with companions, and groups of friends and family. It’s a guarantee for fun in the mud! 😃🐶
course_highlights: Gjørmelabben - an unforgettable event for both individual participants, children with companions, or in teams together with friends and/or family.
Obstacle course for everyone with a dog, all are welcome!
Mud guarantee 😃🐶

name: Grenland Hinderløp
description: Grenland obstacle course gives you the chance to be challenged in new ways and have fun navigating the course at Jarseng. You can look forward to crawling under and over obstacles, balancing, carrying, and rolling in the mud. The level of the course is designed so that everyone can get through, but if an obstacle proves too difficult, you have the option to complete a different task instead. You can choose to participate individually or as part of a team of 3-5 people, and together as a team, you help each other through the obstacles.
course_highlights: You can look forward to crawling under and over obstacles, balancing, carrying, and rolling in the mud.
The level of the course should be such that everyone can get through, but if an obstacle becomes too difficult, you will have the opportunity to do a different task instead.
How about using the obstacle course as a team-building activity at work or to do something fun with your group of friends?

name: Kystjegerløpet
description: Welcome to an unforgettable experience through breathtaking scenery with a finish at the idyllic Sirevåg harbor! The race is approximately 7 km long and suitable for most people. Along the way, you will encounter fun obstacles and tunnels from World War II. You can choose an alternative exercise if an obstacle becomes too challenging. Sign up your team today to experience the adventure for yourself!
course_highlights: The race goes through a fantastic landscape, tunnels from World War II, and finishes in the idyllic Sirevåg harbor.
The course is 7 km long with 17-20 different obstacles.
We arrange the transport of your equipment from start to finish.

name: Grimstad Marathon
description: Grimstad Marathon 2025 will take place on Saturday, September 13, 2025, featuring a new, centrally located, and fast course. No matter the distance, the audience will cheer you on and follow you for much of the way. Choose the distance that suits you best, whether you're running with friends, colleagues, or alone. The course includes 5 km, 10 km, and a half marathon at 21 km, with the start and finish in Byhaven in the Grimstad harbor area, offering a varied experience that includes both sea, forest, and inland scenery.
course_highlights: The course is 5 km and is run one, two, or four times, while the half marathon runners complete an extra loop in the turnaround area to reach 21 km.
The start and finish are in Byhaven in the Grimstad harbor area, and the course takes you past Odden and out along Grooseveien to the Groos bathing area.
No matter which distance you choose, it will be a running celebration with aid stations and cheers throughout the race.

name: Hedersløpet
description: The Honor Run is a unique, slightly different race that brings together all running enthusiasts, both military and civilian, to honor our veterans, both the living and those who have passed away. The race passes by the Memorial Grove and is certified and approved by Kondis as a quality race. It is open to all runners with two distances, 5 km and 10 km, where the 5 km can be walked as a march. The Honor Run was established in 2017 as a joint project by NVIO branch Oslo and several partners, and since then, it has seen increasing participation.
course_highlights: The race honors our veterans, both the living and those who have passed away.
There are two distances, 5 km and 10 km, where the 5 km can be walked as a march.
The project is non-commercial and all profits go to the Veteran Assistance Foundation.

name: Valdresløpet
description: We challenge you to a trail run that truly tests your running capacity and terrain skills in our half marathon. The race takes place on September 13, 2025, and covers a distance of 21.1 km with an elevation gain of 570 m. We hope this course includes everything a trail half marathon should have. The Valdresløpet has been held every year since 1978 and attracts 200-250 participants annually, featuring a varied route from Fagernes to Leirin.
course_highlights: This year's race will take place in new surroundings, starting in the Park at Fagernes and finishing at the Airport in Leirin.
The race is organized in familiar and safe formats with three checkpoints along the way, at Sebufjorden, Storefoss, and Skrautvål kindergarten.
Participants will also receive a running puzzle to solve along the way.

name: Trolljegerprøven Bergen Junior
description: The Troll Hunter Trial Bergen Junior is an exciting obstacle course in Norwegian nature, with a distance of 8 km +. The course features over 30 obstacles, in addition to natural barriers, and is designed so that everyone can participate. Join us for a family-friendly day at Fløien with a 3+ km trail run and 20+ challenging obstacles, perfect for the whole family, groups of friends, and sports teams.
course_highlights: The Troll Hunter Challenge is an 8 km+ long obstacle course in Norwegian nature with 30+ obstacles.
Family Day at Fløien includes a 3+ km trail run with 20+ obstacles for extra challenges.
The race is designed so that everyone can complete it, providing a sense of achievement and fun.

name: Fjordkraft Bergen City Milen
description: It is a pleasure to welcome you to the Fjordkraft Bergen City Mile, a flat 10 km race in the heart of Bergen. The race is held for the seventh time on September 12, 2026, starting at 16:00 from Torgallmenningen. The organizing club TIF Viking invites everyone to another running celebration in the streets of Bergen, and all participants will receive a medal.
course_highlights: There are cash prizes for the top three in the women's and men's categories.
There is also an activity park for children and a Mini-Milen (children's race) of 600 meters.

name: Markus-løpet
description: The Markus Race is now being held for the fifth time and is drawing attention to the gold ribbon, the international symbol for childhood cancer. The proceeds go to childhood cancer research and Cancer Care Rogaland. The race takes place on Saturday, September 13, 2025, with options of a 5 km or 10 km timed race, as well as a 3 km walk/run without timing. Whether you run or walk, you contribute to an important cause while enjoying a unique experience in the beautiful Jæren landscape.
course_highlights: The proceeds go to children's cancer research and Cancer Care Rogaland.
Honorary prizes and awards are distributed in various categories during the event.
Vitengarden/Jærmuseet keeps its entire facility open to everyone in the area.

name: Solidaritetsløp Palestina
description: Solidarity run for Palestine takes place on Saturday, September 13, 2025, starting at 12:00 in Oslo, to raise funds for Palestine. This is a social, active way to show solidarity with Palestine while contributing financially where it is needed most. The course starts and ends in Kubaparken, with running along the Akerselva. Participants can choose between distances of 5 km and 10 km, with those running 10 km completing the 5 km loop twice.
course_highlights: The proceeds from ticket sales go to the Palestinian Red Crescent and the Artificial Limbs and Polio Centre workshop in Gaza.
The Solidarity Run for Palestine aims to be visible in the urban landscape, in the spirit of the running group Run for Palestine Oslo.
The course runs along the beautiful Akerselva, providing participants with a great nature experience while showing solidarity.

name: Kongskleiven Opp
description: Kongskleivo is Bekkjarvik's most popular hike. Here, with the help of a beautiful sherpa path through stunning nature, you will reach the summit of Kongsfjellet, where legends say a king is buried. On the way to the top, you can stop by Taushaugen, where you can catch your breath and enjoy the view over Bekkjarvik. If you're lucky, you might also have a unique encounter with the best wildlife the West Coast has to offer, namely the sea eagle and wild sheep.
course_highlights: Kongskleivo is Bekkjarvik's most popular hike.
You will reach the summit of Kongsfjellet where legends say a king is buried.

name: Lilo Trail
description: LiloTrail is a free and casual half marathon on trails in Lillomarka. The race starts and ends at Solemskogen, which is located in the heart of Lillomarka, and it takes 35 minutes to get there by tram and bus from Oslo S. The course features a varied route that includes downhill sections, paths along water, and climbs to viewpoints. Participants are advised to bring nutrition and water, as there are opportunities to refill along the way.
course_highlights: The race starts and ends at Solemskogen, which is located in the heart of Lillomarka.

The event promises a day filled with fun, challenges, and memories for a lifetime. Join the most bouncy obstacle race of the fall and bring everyone you know!

name: Oslo Maraton 10 km
description: The Oslo Marathon 10 km is part of the BMW Oslo Marathon and has a minimum age requirement of 13 years for participation. There will be several waves with start times from 4:20 PM and onwards, and the maximum time to complete the race is 1 hour and 45 minutes. Participants will pass water stations located approximately every 5 kilometers, and there will be pacers available to help runners achieve their goals.

Both the start and finish for all distances in the BMW Oslo Marathon are at Rådhusplassen in Oslo.

description: Hydro Rundt is a recreational race without classification. The course is 5.0 km, easy to run, and goes around the Hydro Aluminium Karmøy factory area, alternating between gravel and asphalt. Hydro Rundt 2025 will be held this year for the 49th time and will be spring's most beautiful adventure.

Participants can choose to take part with or without timing, and everyone will receive a participation medal. Welcome to the whole family – both two-legged and four-legged!

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, Halvmaraton
description: The Personal Record Race 5 km, 10 km, Half Marathon is an exciting event that offers distances for all types of runners. The course is fast and flat, designed for records, and is AIMS-certified. Participants can enjoy a scenic route while competing, and it’s a great opportunity to gather friends and family for an active day outdoors. Results are available immediately after finishing, and there is free parking.

name: Lina Roindt
description: Lina Roindt is a road race that takes place on September 18, starting and finishing at Torshall in Bolme, Rindal. The competitive runners completed a lap of 10.8 km around Rindal center, while recreational participants could choose between two options: one lap around Rinnvollen (3 km) and one around the center via Sunnabrua (6.7 km). This year, a total of 295 people participated, making it the largest starting field since 1993. Lina Roindt is known as the big family day, with high participation and an efficient recreational committee.
course_highlights: Great participation in the Lina Roindt, with 238 in the fun run category without timing and 25 in the competitive categories, totaling 263 participants.
42 of the participants lined up in the starting field that raced for time, the largest starting field since 1993.
There was excitement about whether Strindheim runner Ebrahim Abdulaziz could break the nearly 30-year-old course record set by Dag Øxnvad.

name: Frogn på langs
description: Frogn Longways 2025 takes place on Sunday, September 14, and is a cultural hiking march and trail run for the whole family. The route goes through varying forest and cultural landscapes via historical sites in Frogn, providing a great opportunity to get to know the municipality. Drinks will be served at five checkpoints, but it is recommended to bring your own drinks and packed lunch for those who wish to complete the entire route. Participants can choose to start from Ramme or Follo Museum, and the trail run starts at 10:00 AM with distances of 10 or 28 km.
course_highlights: The route goes through varying forest and cultural landscapes via historical sites in Frogn, and is a great opportunity to get to know our beautiful municipality.
Drinks will be served at the five refreshment stations, but we still recommend that you, as a walker, bring your own drinks and packed lunch.
Frogn along the way is a massive public health initiative, and the organizers have put in a lot of effort to ensure that participants can enjoy top-notch trails.

The children's race starts at 10:00 AM, and all participants receive a medal. The mass start for the 5 km and 10 km races is at 11:00 AM. The entry fee is 250 NOK for non-members, while Moov members participate for free.

The race takes place on Sunday, September 15, 2024, at 1:00 PM from Dokka Stadium.

name: Seterløpet
description: Seterløpet, Norway's oldest race, is organized from Solumsmoen in Sigdal to Vestre Spone Sports Ground. The race, which is 18.5 km long, has a mass start for competitive runners at 11:00 AM, while recreational runners can start from 9:00 AM. There is organized transportation from Vestre Spone Sports Ground at around 9:30 AM, and registration takes place at the start. This race is a collaboration between Nedre Sigdal Sports Club and Vestre Spone IF.
course_highlights: The Seterløpet was first held in 1936 and is thus Norway's oldest race.
The race has a mass start for the competitive class at 11:00 AM, while recreational runners can start from 9:00 AM.

name: Bryneløpet
description: This year's Bryneløp takes place on Saturday, September 13, during the Potato Festival (September 12-14). The race is organized for children in elementary school (grades 1-7) and has been held since 2013. Participants start in groups for grades 1-2, grades 3-4, and grades 5-7 for both girls and boys. The course starts between M44 and Brynesenteret and goes around the lower part of Fritz Røed Park, in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: The Bryne Race is a popular event that takes place in picturesque surroundings.
Participants can look forward to a varied and exciting course that takes them through both forests and open landscapes.
The race has several distances to choose from, making it accessible for both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Stoltzekleiven Opp
description: Stoltzekleiven Opp is a race that has been part of the running calendar since 1979. The event takes place in Bergen and is known for being a challenging uphill climb. Participants get to experience a spectacular course that takes them up the steep Stoltzekleiven, a historic staircase with 722 steps. The race has a strong focus on community and includes both individual participants and groups, and it is organized every year in September by the sports club Varegg.
course_highlights: Stoltzekleiven Opp is reportedly the world's largest uphill race, with about 6,300 participants in recent years.
The race has an elevation gain of 301.44 meters and goes over approximately 800 steps.
The event spans two days, starting on Friday and Saturday of the last weekend in September from 9:15 AM to 6:15 PM each day.

name: Hodlekve Rundt Fjelløp
description: Join the ultimate mountain race in Hodlekve, featuring races of 21, 10, and 6 km in beautiful terrain. This is an activity day for both young and old, with partners like Rab and Intersport contributing with activities and great offers. The race starts and finishes at Dalalåven, with the starting gun for the 21 km at 10:00 and for the 10 km and 6 km at 10:30. The junior race and treasure hunt will begin after 10:30, and Dalalåven will have an open café with food and drink service.
course_highlights: Choose a beautiful round trip of about 21 km and 1000 meters of elevation over two mountains, a slightly shorter route of about 10 km and 500 meters of elevation, or a hiking trail of 6 km.
The secretariat is open in Dalalåven from 9:00 AM, and it is allowed to go out on the course to cheer for the runners.
At Dalalåven, there will be activities all day with maps and descriptions made available well in advance of the race.

description: CrazyRace is fun for the whole family, and the race is suitable for adults and children from 4 years old, regardless of experience or fitness level. You can run or walk at your own pace, and there are many fun and challenging obstacles along the way. Crazy Race Skedsmo is returning this fall, so bring the whole family and jump around on all our obstacles!
course_highlights: The race is suitable for adults and children from 4 years old, regardless of experience or fitness level.
You can run or walk at your own pace, and there are many fun and challenging obstacles along the way.
Crazy Race Skedsmo has 14 enormous inflatable obstacles that you won't want to miss!

name: Fýri Trail by Salomon
description: Fýri Trail By Salomon is happy to invite you to the final of the Salomon Golden Trail Nordic Series. Experience the magic of Scandinavia's finest trails with two distances: 29 km and 18 km. This race will test your trail skills and provide you with an incredible experience as you run along the mountain trails of Hemsedal, where you will discover technical paths, steep ascents, and untouched wilderness.
course_highlights: Two stages, the same superhero feeling at the finish line!
Discover everything from technical trails to steep hills and untouched wilderness.
Run along the shores of some beautiful lakes and explore some of the best trails Norway has to offer.

name: Flyplassmila
description: The Airport Mile 2025 will be held on Saturday, September 20, 2025, and is known for having the "world's fastest course" on the runway of Stord Airport, Sørstokken. The course is almost completely flat and has a straight direction, providing optimal conditions for setting personal records. Participants can choose between the distances of 5 kilometers and 10 kilometers, with certified and officially measured courses.
course_highlights: The course layout is on the runway at Stord Airport, with turns resembling an indoor athletics track, 11m radius/22m diameter.
One lap is 2.5 kilometers, and the course shows a total elevation gain of 7 meters on Strava.
Race numbers can be picked up at the terminal at the airport from 10:00 AM, so please be there in good time!

name: Trail Monkey
description:
Unleash your inner TrailMonkey! 

Are you ready to play through nature like a true TrailMonkey? Monkeytrail is not like other races – it’s a celebration of freedom, movement, and playfulness. Here, it’s not just about kilometers and seconds, but about muddy shoes, grins under fir trees, and the feeling of being wildly alive.

Your adventure awaits...

Choose between two epic courses:

    6KM Trail – perfect for those who want to challenge themselves in hilly, playful terrain.

    12KM Tough Monkey Edition – for those who can’t get enough of hills, slopes, and forest magic.

    18KM MonKey Banan – for those who want to go all in: more running, more mud, more madness. And maybe a banana at the finish line.

Run, climb, laugh – and become part of something bigger...

MonkeyTrail is made for both everyday heroes and wilderness veterans. Here we celebrate movement in nature – whether you leap over roots like a ninja monkey or take your time while inhaling forest air like a Zen monk on caffeine.

You don’t need top speed; you need a sense of adventure. And maybe a little balance.

Nature's superpowers (and why you become magical by participating)

    You get a better mood just by tying your shoelaces.

    The trees give you a free mental reboot.

    Every hill you conquer grants you +10 self-respect and +5 smiles.

    And mud? Well, it’s nature’s beauty treatment for the soul.

Medal for EVERYONE – Because you are a true TrailMonkey

Everyone who finishes receives the legendary TrailMonkey medal – proof that you master the terrain and dare to play. The winners are rewarded with honor, glory, and prizes – but everyone is rewarded with nature’s applause and a solid sense of achievement.

Join us!

Become part of the pack. Run and laugh. 
Monkeytrail – it’s not just a race. 
It’s the freedom in a pair of trail shoes.
course_highlights: Our events are made for everyone - from 5 km beginners to ultra marathon warriors - and are designed with inclusivity and boundary-breaking ideas in mind.
Navigate our well-marked trails safely with support from our experienced team, and feel the energy from our close-knit, supportive running community.
At the finish line, you celebrate your achievements not only with a medal but with a warm welcome from the community, and yes, some good old tea and cake!

name: Hauernløpet
description: The Hauernløpet is a trail race of 19 km that mostly takes place on paths, with sections of gravel, through beautiful areas in Drammensmarka. The first five kilometers have an approximately 50/50 distribution between paths and gravel, while the next segment is almost exclusively on paths until 15 km. From 15 to 17 km, there is more gravel than path, before it returns to paths for the final stretch to the finish line. In total, there is about 75% path and 25% gravel.
course_highlights: The Hauern Race is a 19 km trail run.
The race goes through beautiful areas in Drammensmarka.
Overall, about 75% of the route is on trail and 25% on gravel.

name: Fædrelandsvennen Stafetten
description: The FVN Relay 2025 is organized by the Agder Corporate Sports Association in collaboration with Fædrelandsvennen. There will be competitions in mixed, women's, and men's categories, focusing on the joy of running, community, and team building. Each category consists of three legs, with each leg being approximately 2.2 km. The event will take place on Saturday, September 20, in Tresse, Kristiansand, and there will also be a separate active category for the fittest women and men participating in the mass start.
course_highlights: Emphasis is placed on the joy of running, community, and team building.
Each leg is approximately 2.2 km, and there are three legs per team.
There will be a separate active class for the fittest women and men who run the first mass start.

name: Stjernemila
description: The Stjernemila is a running event that starts in the center of Flekkefjord, right in the middle of the festivities! The course is approximately 10 kilometers long and follows a star-shaped route from the finish area, with six "arms" that take you to iconic locations in the center. The course is well-marked, and participants can have their leg times recorded on the big screen, providing the audience with a good overview. The event includes both the main race and a relay, as well as free children's races for the age groups 3-7 years and 8-12 years.
course_highlights: The runners take off in a star shape from the finish area, heading out into the 6 "arms" of the star, each of which is an iconic location in the center of Flekkefjord.
The course includes quite a few hills to reach the viewpoints, but it's no more than about 200 meters of elevation.
The Star Mile is more than just a race; the center will be buzzing with life and activities for both young and old, with exciting menus at the city's many outdoor venues in the evening.

name: Oppdalsløpet
description: The traditional Oppdal Race kicks off on Saturday, September 21 at 1:00 PM! The Oppdal Race is a 3.5 km long trail run, along gravel roads and paths, with the start and finish at the NOIL square. There is an opportunity to both run and walk, and the race is suitable for all ages. Pre-registration is possible until midnight on September 20, while late registration takes place on Saturday, September 21 between 12:00 and 12:30 at NOIL. Registration is free, and a trophy will be awarded to the fastest woman and man. Welcome!
course_highlights: The race is free, and there is an option for both running and walking.
Trophy for the fastest woman and man.
The Oppdal Race is part of the Oppdal Weekend, along with the bazaar in the NOIL house.

name: Kristiansand Backyard Ultra
description: The laps start every full hour, and your pace determines how long your break is before the next start. Although the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, you are warmly welcome to run as many laps as you wish – or can manage. For us at Backyard Norway, running is not about showing off or the pursuit of being the best, but about overcoming oneself and pushing new boundaries. Regardless of whether this boundary is at 10, 25, or 80 km, all runners are welcome, and the last participant to finish has performed just as strongly as the first.
course_highlights: The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start.
Even though the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, you are warmly welcome to run as many laps as you want – or can manage.
Running is a lifestyle and a leisure activity, and we want to challenge ourselves and push new boundaries.

name: Kongeløpet
description: The King’s Race is a recreational run that goes from Byrknesøy to Skjerjehamn. The race covers a distance of 13 km, over bridges and islands, on asphalt in beautiful coastal scenery. Just hilly enough to be challenging.
additional:
The King’s Race is a recreational run that goes from Joker on Byrknesøy to Skjerjehamn on Sandøy. It is a collaborative project between Ytre Gulen Sports Club and Skjerjehamn. There are 3 water stations along the route. Organizers assist with the transport of equipment from the starting point to the finish line.

Entry fee for the race number is 150,-.
course_highlights: Varied selection of distances from 0.5 km to 13 km.
The race takes place in picturesque surroundings in Øvre Eiker.
Suitable for both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Skeikampen Opp
description: Skeikampen Opp is a mountain race from the base of Skeikampen to the stone hut at the top. The race is suitable for both active athletes and recreational runners of all ages, so there's no excuse not to participate. It is 2.9 km long and consists of 340 meters of elevation gain. You can choose which category you want to compete in, with a recreational category for those who do not wish to be timed. The competitive categories start in waves according to age from 12:00 PM.
course_highlights: The race takes place in scenic surroundings from the foot of Skeikampen to the stone cabin at the top!
You can choose to start between 11:00 AM and 11:30 AM if you are participating in the recreational class.
The competition classes start in waves based on age, with the first start at 12:00 PM for men aged 17 to 49.

This race offers a unique experience in coastal nature and includes several distances for all levels.
course_highlights: The first edition of Hvalermila was held in 2021 - welcome to the fifth edition in 2025!
Join the autumn running festival in stunning nature.
We at Hvaler IL want to organize a race that is at least as fantastic as the Hvaler Race.

description: Join us for a run around the beautiful Trommedalen at the Bondemarknaden in Etne. Monica Hundseid will participate in the race, which has a distance of approximately 8.2 km. In October, the Bondespretten race was organized to raise funds for the organization Mat onna bronå in Haugesund, and a total of 3,000 kroner was collected from the entry fees.

Stine Hatteberg was the only woman to complete the race, with a time of 19:01. For the family and recreational class, the start was at Skarveland school between 10:00 AM and 11:00 AM, with no timing.

The 5 km course has been adapted for 2024, with fewer hills and a more runnable terrain.

The 10 km race takes place around Edlandsvatnet and finishes on the track at the finish line.
The 5 km course starts on the track and has been modified to be more accessible for all participants.

description: On Sunday, September 22 at 12 PM, the Schjongtest is being held for the 8th time, with the motto for the day: "It's okay to have fun!" Last year, 311 people participated, and the event includes two children's races of 600 m and 1700 m, as well as a competitive class/recreational run with or without timing at 1700 m. The course is marked with signs every 100 m, and at 11:45 AM, Andy will start his fun and energetic warm-up, suitable for everyone. Bring family, friends, neighbors, and colleagues for a shared experience in beautiful Schjongslunden.
course_highlights: The Schjong test offers many beautiful unconventional and traditional prizes that can entice both the eyes and the stomach.
The 1700 m course is marked with signs every 100 m.
At 11:45, Andy will start his fun and energetic warm-up, suitable for everyone.

name: Bergen 5000 Challenge
description: Bergen 5000 Challenge takes place on Sunday, September 22, 2024, starting at 5:00 PM at Fana Stadium. Challenge yourself, friends, family, colleagues, or teams to the fastest 5000m race of the fall in Bergen, consisting of 12.5 laps without inclines. The race offers recreational and elite classes, with pacers to support the participants. Admission is free for the audience, so bring everyone you know and cheer on the runners to create a great atmosphere.
course_highlights: The successful first edition of the Bergen 5000 challenge was held with a 5000m race for both recreational runners and elites, as well as a 1000m children's race.
A total of 116 participants were registered, and Gneist provided pacers in all heats to help the runners achieve good times.
The race is open to both experienced runners and beginners, providing a great opportunity to experience the community of running enthusiasts.

name: Slitusprinten
description: The Slitusprint, organized by Slitu IF Skigruppe, invites runners and recreational athletes aged 11 and up to a fast-paced 10 km road race in Slitu on Sunday, September 28, 2025, as well as a trial Norwegian Championship on 5 km. The course is officially measured by NFIF and is record-fast, featuring only asphalt as the surface and flat terrain, making it easy to run. The start and finish are at Slitu Stadium, and parking will be at Morenen Shopping Center. Timing and registration will be handled through EQ-Timing, with race number pickup on race day from 10 AM to 12:30 PM.
course_highlights: The course is officially measured by NFIF and is record fast!
With only asphalt as the surface and flat terrain, the course is easy to run and straightforward.
There were strong times and personal bests in the very fast 10 km course, despite the wind conditions.

The run takes place on Mondays starting at 7 PM.
The event is open to joggers and runners from 9 years old.

Asker Ski Club is pleased to invite you to this race, which starts at 6:00 PM in Asker Park.
course_highlights: The event invites both experienced runners and beginners to participate.

Asker Ski Club is the organizer of the Føyka Terrain.

name: Ringshaugløpet
description: RINGSHAUGLØPET is a low-threshold race where you can test your fitness or just get a good workout. The race is organized 2-4 times a year and is open to everyone. The loop at Vallø is run counterclockwise, and the course is on asphalt the entire way. It is open to traffic, and timing is done with a personal watch. Participants report their completion or time.
course_highlights: The race is held 2-4 times a year, and it is open to everyone.
The lap at Vallø is run counterclockwise, and the course is on asphalt all the way.

name: Vom Dogrun - Kristiansand
description: The wait is over! VOM Dogrun is returning to Kristiansand and hosting a real dog party at Tresse outside Christiansholm Fortress. Join us for a social and fun outing with your dog, in the company of other dog lovers. You can choose to participate with or without timing, and there will be a participation medal for everyone. Welcome to the whole family – both two-legged and four-legged!
course_highlights: Everyone receives a medal and participant prize, including a beautiful Vom dog bowl and a race number.
VOM PUPPY WALK is a special activity for puppies – which is free to sign up for.
The competition class allows only one dog and one person per bib number with timing, while in the Open class, multiple dogs per person are permitted.

name: RUNFEST
description: Get ready for Runfest Norway – the world's most ambitious three-day street running festival. The event takes place from October 1 to 3, 2026, in Sandnes – the hometown of Olympic champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen – and offers a unique combination of elite competition and the joy of running in fantastic surroundings here on the edge of Norway. RUNFEST aims to be a unique, global event that inspires joy in running, better health, diversity, and community.
course_highlights: The event offers a unique combination of elite competition and the joy of running in fantastic surroundings.
The goal of RUNFEST is to place Sandnes and the region clearly on the map, both nationally and internationally.
RUNFEST embraces Team Ingebrigtsen's desire to inspire better health and community.

name: Ogndal KM Terrengløp Lang
description: Ogndal KM Cross Country Long is an exciting cross country race taking place in beautiful Ogndal. name: Stavanger Backyard
description: Backyard Stavanger is a backyard ultra that takes place in late September each year. It follows the classic backyard formula where all participants run laps of 6.7 km every hour, and you must be ready for a new lap before the next one starts in order to continue. A maximum of 12 laps can be run, which corresponds to 50 miles or 80 kilometers. The fastest runner on the 12th lap is considered the winner of the race, and the times before this do not matter. The course is partly gravel and partly asphalt, so it is important to dress appropriately and be prepared for changing weather conditions.

The race continues until there is only one participant left who completes a lap. Although the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, everyone is welcome to run as many laps as they wish – or can handle. In 2026, the race will take place at Nordre Nattlandsfjellet in Bergen, Hordaland.

name: Tekna Veldedighetsløp
description:
The charity run is being organized for the second year in a row and will take place on September 28th. This year, just like last year, we want to highlight the importance of students' mental health. Mental health is a topic that never goes out of date, and we must continue to work on it so that we can constantly improve our ability to tackle the challenges that everyday life presents to us.

We want to support and shed light on the services provided by Mental Helse Ungdom with the funds we manage to raise. The registration fee paid upon signing up goes entirely to Mental Helse Ungdom.

Although we are running to benefit students' mental health, we want to invite adults of all ages to join in and run. The course will be set around the large Lungegårdsvann – a distance that is manageable regardless of fitness level. Participants can choose whether they want to run, walk, or contribute as cheerleaders.

Join us and use your legs for a good cause!

You'll be cheered on along the route by many spectators with flags and music, making it perhaps the most enjoyable race of the year to be a part of.

It consists of two loops of 5 km each, providing a more spectator-friendly and traffic-safe course. The start for the Norway Race 5 km is at 11:00, while the 10 km starts at 12:00, followed by the children's race at 12:10.

name: Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M
description: Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M is a running competition organized according to the "Backyard" principle, originating from Big's Backyard Ultra in Tennessee, USA. The course is 6706 meters long and must be completed once every hour; anyone who fails to meet the deadline for the next start is out. The competition has a maximum duration of 12 hours, allowing for a maximum distance of 80467 meters, equivalent to nearly two marathons. The winner is determined by the fastest time on the last lap if multiple participants finish.
course_highlights: The course is 6706 meters long, and it is necessary to complete one lap every hour in order to continue in the competition.
The maximum distance in the Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M is 80,467 meters, which is just over 8 miles.
The winner is determined by the fastest time on the last lap if multiple participants complete the same number of laps.

name: Kruke's Ultra-Trail Challenge
description: Kruke's Ultra-Trail Challenge (KUTC) challenges you to run a loop from Saksvik to Solemsvåttan as many times as possible within given time limits. Test your own limits! Complete it 4 times to participate in the 'fun run', 7 times to become a true ultra-runner (> 42.2 km), and 8, 12, or 15 times to reach classic ultra distances of 50 km, 50 miles, or 100 km. Do it 24 times to run 100 miles, climb Mount Everest... and become a legend! The race takes place on the third Saturday in October, but deviations may occur.

name: Nøklevann Rundt
description: Nøklevann Rundt was held for the 43rd time on Saturday, October 12, 2024. The race has usually been blessed with brilliant weather, but this year, the weather gods were not on the organizer's or participants' side. The rain started around the same time as the 5-kilometer race, and the cold downpour only intensified throughout the afternoon. However, the racing conditions were OK with the right gear, and many strong times were achieved. As usual, the event was smoothly guided to port by the experienced and friendly staff.
course_highlights: Nøklevann Rundt is a short, easy, and child-friendly hike in a popular outdoor area in Østmarka.
The race takes you past beautiful swimming spots like Ulsrudvannet and Rustadsaga, where there are opportunities to enjoy the sun and water.
It is a beautiful route with historical roads such as Sarabråtveien, established in 1856, and Korketrekkeren, which provides a unique experience of the Marka.

name: Fredrikstad Maraton

The first half of the course is on asphalt, while the rest is on gravel and forest roads in Fredrikstadmarka. The course has been the same since the start of the Fredrikstad Marathon in 2001, and both the start and finish are at the FIF house at Ilaveien 132 in Fredrikstad. The lap takes the runners south towards the city, before they turn around and run back through scenic areas to the FIF house.
